note: Cluster assignment for the blast-radius ranking (design spec §8.2). A cluster is a ROOT
CAUSE -- the unit a fix actually ships in -- not a topic. Every assignment below is taken
from the register's own `**Root-cause group**:` line on that entry in §2, quoted verbatim
in `registerSource`. Nothing here is a fresh diagnosis; §3 states plainly that grouping
errors are cheap to make and expensive to act on, so this file makes them arguable instead
of implicit.
PARTITION RULE. `aggregate` sums a cluster over its members, so an entry in two clusters
would be counted twice. Where the register names two groups for one entry it names them in
order (`G5 + G3`, `G8 / G4`); the FIRST is taken as the assignment and the second is carried
in `alternate` and printed beside the entry. Where the register says `Recorded as Gn`, that
is the assignment.
WHOLE-ENTRY RULE. Counts are per entry, not per lane, so a cluster sum attributes an
entry's WHOLE frequency to one cluster even where the register splits the entry across two
by lane (R-23, R-28). This is a known over-attribution and is disclosed in the ranking.
ONLY SILENT ENTRIES APPEAR HERE (spec §8.1). The ranking's generator fails if this file
assigns an entry the regenerated §0.2 does not measure SILENT, or omits one it does.

ADDED 2026-09-08 at `b13c890330` (off `dde0f083c0`, the branch base, which carries no entry)
by the register-property-key-followups branch: R-57 and
R-58, each with its own singleton CLUSTER DEFINITION as well as its assignment, because a
singleton has no other member to hang on -- the mirror image of the R-56 removal above.
Both entries' `**Root-cause group**:` lines say `unclustered`, and both say WHY at length;
the quotes below are elided in the R-47 style, not paraphrased.
THE TWO ARE NOT MERGED INTO ONE CLUSTER, AND THAT IS A DECISION, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. They
share a real shape: both are `kali_parser` converting a literal's SOURCE TEXT with Rust's
grammar where JavaScript's is required -- `unquote_string_literal` not decoding escapes,
and `numeric_property_name` parsing `042` as decimal. Merging them would have been the
tidier ranking. It is declined on this file's OWN definition: a cluster is a ROOT CAUSE,
`the unit a fix actually ships in`. Escape decoding and legacy-octal value conversion live
in different functions, need different tests, and cannot land in one change -- and R-58's
fix additionally has to answer a strict-mode question that has nothing to do with escapes.
Naming a new section-3 group for the family would be a fresh diagnosis, which section 3
opens by warning is cheap to make and expensive to act on; the shape claim is recorded in
both register entries instead, so a later reader can form the group on evidence.
R-58 DECLINES G3 EXPLICITLY, and the reason is worth reading before anyone re-files it
there. It has G3's shape more exactly than most G3 members do -- the guard (`042n` refused
for its leading zero) and the hole (`042` walked past) are three lines apart in one
nine-line function. It is declined because section 3's remedy for G3 is to replace the
denylist with an allowlist at the choke point, and here that remedy is WRONG: refusing
`042` would make kali reject a program node RUNS, trading a silent wrong value for a loud
regression. The alternate reading is recorded on the assignment, as R-47's is.
ADDED 2026-09-08 at `02297ca6c2` by the same branch, second pair: R-59 and R-60, which
complete the four
divergences PR #34 measured and left unfiled. THESE TWO ARE NOT BOTH SINGLETONS, which
breaks the pattern of the three entries above. R-59 takes its own singleton CLUSTER
DEFINITION as well as an assignment; R-60 joins the EXISTING G6, so it adds an assignment
and no definition. Both `**Root-cause group**:` lines are quoted below in the R-47 style,
elided and not paraphrased.
R-59 DECLINES G1, AND THE DECLINE IS THE INTERESTING PART. G1 is named `parser fail-open
recovery`, and `fails open where it should decline` is R-59 in five words -- but G1's own
Members and Traced bullets define it by a MECHANISM, a parser position whose contract with
the token STREAM is wrong (a discarded `accept`, a non-consuming closer). Nothing
desynchronizes in R-59: `expression_to_property_name` consumes no tokens at all, so G1's
standing recommendation -- sweep every `let _ = self.stream.accept` -- would walk straight
past it. Section 3's G1 already carries a warning about exactly this move: R-43 was listed
there on a name-level match and is now labelled INFERRED because no site was ever traced.
R-59's site IS traced, and it is not a stream site. The alternate reading is recorded on
the assignment.
R-60 IS THE FIRST ENTRY THIS BRANCH FILED THAT JOINS A CLUSTER RATHER THAN DECLINING ONE,
and it joins on measurement. Section 3's G6 asks for one experiment to raise its
confidence -- `call any other plausible-but-absent builtin and observe whether it yields 0
or E3100` -- and filing R-60 ran it. The answer is BOTH, and the E3100 is a warning that
`kali run` never shows: `Object.fromEntries` reaches codegen unresolved and is lowered
through the zero-placeholder call fallback whose own message says so. G6's shipped remedy
is a value-builtin deny-set at `emit_call`'s terminal fallback, and this call is simply
not on it, so the fix ships with G6's -- which is this file's test. G2 is named and
declined on the assignment: G2's members are all USER function values, and a missing
builtin is what G6 exists to hold.
R-59 IS THE FIRST NONZERO COUNT ADDED TO THIS FILE SINCE THE FREEZE. R-57, R-58 and R-60
all measure raw 0 / reachable 0 and move no other cluster's band; R-59 measures raw 302 /
reachable 45 -- the same four figures R-13's matcher prints. Because the two entries are in
DIFFERENT clusters -- R-13 in G3, R-59 a singleton -- `aggregate` counts the sites they
share once under each. That is a real over-attribution of the same kind the WHOLE-ENTRY
RULE above discloses, it is disclosed here and in `count.mjs`'s UPPER_BOUNDS, and it is not
resolved by moving either entry: R-59's own entry records that R-13's G3 assignment rested
on a mechanism hypothesis R-59 disproves, and says that re-clustering an existing entry is
not a filing task's decision.
CORRECTED 2026-09-08 (review round 1): this paragraph said the overlap was `by construction
(R-59's matcher is a strict subset of R-13's shape)`. THAT IS FALSE, and the instrument
disproves it in one line. `var o={}; o[true]; o[null]; o[/x/]; o[1n];` counts 0 under
`computedMemberNonLiteralKey` and 4 under `computedMemberFabricatedPropertyName` (literals
the parser cannot READ); `var o={1:"one"}; o[(1)]; o[(0,1)]; o[+1]; o[-1];` counts 3 under
the first and 0 under the second (readable non-literals). The two OVERLAP AND NEITHER
CONTAINS THE OTHER, both directions are counted correctly, and the identical corpus figures
mean only that the corpus contains NEITHER separating family. The double-counting warning
above is unaffected -- it never depended on containment, only on the sites the two do share.
CORRECTED AGAIN 2026-09-08 (final review): the paragraph above says R-59 measures raw 302 /
reachable 45, `the same four figures R-13's matcher prints`. THAT WAS TRUE WHEN WRITTEN AND
IS NO LONGER TRUE, and it is left standing as the record of what was published. R-59's
matcher was counting assignment and update TARGETS, which R-59's own entry measures are not
the defect -- `o[i] = 8` leaves `o.i` at `7` on both engines and `o[i]++` is refused LOUDLY
at exit 1 -- so it now counts READS ONLY, as R-60's matcher already did. R-59 measures raw
235 / reachable 27 (anchor 27/25, extension 208/2), and the deltas are exactly R-13's
record's own breakdown storeTarget figures (raw 67, reachable 18). Measured over the frozen
corpus file by file: of the 51 files with a nonzero count under either matcher, 30 now
differ (8 of the 14 reachable ones), and R-59's count exceeds R-13's in ZERO files -- so on
THIS CORPUS R-59's sites are a strict subset of R-13's, which is a fact about the corpus and
still not containment between the shapes. The double-counting warning survives unchanged in
substance and is now PARTIAL rather than total: a reader must still not add the two counts.
